## Baños in 2 Days: Quilotoa and Ecuador's Waterfalls

[Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) lies in a green Andean valley near Tungurahua Volcano. The town is known for its cascading waterfalls, hot springs, and outdoor adventures. This Ada Tours excursion combines the natural scenery around Baños with a visit to Quilotoa Crater Lake.

**Duration: 2 days and 1 night.** This is a standalone itinerary with a Russian-speaking guide and transfers along the route. The trip begins in Baños; a transfer from Quito is not included.

## Day One: Quilotoa Crater Lake

One of the main highlights is **Quilotoa**, a crater lake surrounded by Andean mountains. Its water can appear turquoise or greenish, and the upper rim offers a sweeping panorama. A trail descends to the shore, but the climb back at altitude requires physical effort.

On this route, it is important to consider not only the time needed to descend but also the effort of returning uphill. Some travelers prefer to stay at the upper viewpoint; discuss whether to make the descent in advance. A separate [excursion to Quilotoa from Quito](/ecuador/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/quilotoa-lake-from-quito/) suits those who are not planning to spend a night in Baños.

Participants in the two-day program should agree in advance on the timing of the longer drives and the time spent at the lake: actual driving times depend on the weather and road conditions.

## Day Two: The Town and the Waterfall Route

The itinerary includes exploring Baños and visiting its waterfalls. You will see **Agoyán**, **Manto de la Novia (Bride's Veil)**, and **Pailón del Diablo (Devil's Cauldron)**.

Pailón del Diablo is striking for its powerful flow surrounded by cliffs and lush, damp vegetation. The local viewing paths can be wet, so shoes with good grip are essential. At Manto de la Novia, the itinerary includes a cable-car ride. Confirm the actual access arrangements and whether the specific ticket is included: the general list of included services for this trip mentions only the guide and transfers.

The waterfall stops reveal how mountain landscapes give way to wetter, greener valleys. This natural part of the journey deserves enough time, rather than rushing between viewpoints simply to take photographs.

## The Swing at the End of the World and Outdoor Activities

The itinerary also offers a chance to visit the famous **Swing at the End of the World**, with views across the mountain valley. The view and the opportunity to ride depend on local rules, weather, and the time of your visit.

A **zipline over the Pastaza River canyon** is available separately. This is an optional activity, costing an additional **$15 per person**, and it is **not included in the base price**.

Other adventure activities available around Baños should not automatically be assumed to be included in this two-day package.

## What's Included and What's Extra

**Included:** a Russian-speaking guide and transfers during the itinerary.

**Not included:** 1 night of hotel accommodation, medical insurance, and the optional zipline at $15 per person. The specific hotel option and any additional admission tickets should be agreed in advance.

### Prices by Group Size

| Group | Price |
|---|---|
| Stated base rate | $1065 |
| Group of 2 | $585 per person |
| Group of 3 | $548 per person |
| Group of 4 | $495 per person |

The base amount of $1065 does not specify the same pricing unit as the group rates. It should therefore be kept separate, with its applicable conditions clarified. For the other options, the price per person varies with group size.

## Weather and Practical Advice

Baños sits in a mountain valley with a humid climate. Bring a lightweight rain layer, closed-toe shoes, and clothing suitable for walks near waterfalls. Extra warm clothing will be useful for the high-altitude visit to Quilotoa.

If travelers have mobility or physical-exertion limitations, discuss viewpoint access and alternatives to difficult descents in advance. Discover more trips in the [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/) and the [Nature section](/interests/nature/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Two-Day Baños Tour

### How long is the trip?

**2 days and 1 night**, traveling via Quilotoa and the waterfalls around Baños.

### Is the hotel included?

No. One night of hotel accommodation is explicitly listed as an exclusion.

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide?

Yes. Russian-language guiding and transfers are included in the program.

### Is the zipline included in the price?

No. It is a separate activity costing **$15 per person**.

## Baños Waterfalls and Return to Quito in One Day

[Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) lies in a green Andean valley near Tungurahua Volcano. The town makes a convenient starting point for the Waterfall Route: within a relatively short stretch of the Pastaza River valley, you can see several different cascades, gorges, and viewpoints.

**This itinerary starts in Baños and ends in Quito.** That distinction matters when choosing your route: this is a full sightseeing day ending with a transfer to the capital, not a short circular excursion that departs from Quito and immediately returns to its starting point.

Including stops and transfers, the day takes **11–12 hours**, with the drive from Baños to Quito accounting for about **3.5 hours**. Allow enough time for the final transfer: the waterfalls, walks, and swing occupy only part of the day.

## Which Waterfalls Are on the Route?

The journey brings together several well-known attractions that reveal different sides of the Pastaza Valley:

- [**Agoyán**](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/) — a powerful waterfall beside the road, with clear views of the gorge's depth and the surrounding greenery.
- [**Manto de la Novia (Bride's Veil)**](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) — a narrow white stream dropping down the slope; the itinerary includes a stop with a cable car.
- [**Pailón del Diablo (Devil's Cauldron)**](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/) — a cascade framed by steep cliffs, reached along walking paths.

All these stops are connected with [Pastaza Canyon](/ecuador/place/pastaza-canyon/). Unlike a conventional city sightseeing tour, this nature-focused journey involves walking, descents, and sections where spray from the waterfalls reaches the paths.

Not every famous Baños activity forms part of the paid excursion. Rafting, bungee jumping, cycling routes, and thermal pools are associated with the region, but they are not listed as mandatory elements of this particular trip.

## The Swing at the End of the World vs. the Canopy Zipline

Another stop is [**Casa del Árbol**](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/), home to the Swing at the End of the World above a mountainside. Visitors can ride the swing. Admission arrangements, weather restrictions, and queues depend on the venue's operations.

You can also consider the **canopy zipline over Pastaza Canyon**. This aerial activity on a cable requires different preparation from walking between viewpoints. The canopy zipline **is not included in the price** and costs an additional **$15 per person**. Participation is optional.

Travelers who prefer to avoid extreme activities can still enjoy the route without the zipline: the main waterfall stops, Pastaza Valley, and Baños itself remain substantial parts of the day.

## Before the Return Journey

After breakfast at the hotel, the program includes a short walk through central Baños before setting off for the waterfalls. For the outdoor sections, bring closed-toe, nonslip shoes, a light raincoat or windbreaker, water, and protection for cameras and phones against spray.

Wet paths and stairs call for care. Travelers who find lengthy walks or descending steps difficult should discuss which stops are accessible before the trip. Even small groups may move along the trails at different speeds.

**The final leg is the return to [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/).** Allow about 3.5 hours for the transfer. If you have a flight or another onward connection that evening, factor in possible delays on the mountain road; the stated duration does not guarantee an exact arrival time.

## Who Is This Excursion For, and Which Baños Itinerary Should You Choose?

This program suits travelers who **are already in Baños** and want to finish exploring the surrounding area before heading to Quito. In one day, you can see several waterfalls, part of the canyon, and panoramas from Casa del Árbol.

For more time in the region, thermal pools, or additional adventure activities, compare this route with the [two-day Baños program](/ecuador/banos/banos-tour-from-quito-2-days/). The best choice depends mainly on how many days you have and whether you need to return to the capital after the excursion.

The excursion combines [adventure](/interests/adventure/) and [Ecuador's natural landscapes](/interests/wildlife/), but physical demands can be discussed separately: walking stops and the canopy zipline are very different activities.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Waterfall Route from Baños

### Does the excursion start in Quito?

No. This program features walks and excursions departing from Baños, with **Quito as the final destination of the return transfer**.

### How long does the entire day take?

**11–12 hours including transfers.** The Baños–Quito transfer takes about 3.5 hours.

### Which waterfalls do we visit?

The route includes **Agoyán**, **Manto de la Novia**, and **Pailón del Diablo**, with nature stops around Pastaza Canyon.

### Is the canopy zipline included in the price?

No. It is an optional activity with a separate price of **$15 per person**.

### Can I skip extreme activities?

Yes. The main waterfalls, the town walk, and the valley views remain part of the route even if you opt out of the canopy zipline.

[Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) lies among Ecuador's green slopes, not far from Tungurahua Volcano. Its Waterfall Route follows Pastaza Canyon and links several powerful cascades. The [“Baños: Waterfalls and Swing, Returning to Quito” excursion](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) includes a tour of the town, Agoyán, Manto de la Novia and Pailón del Diablo waterfalls, the canyon, and the Swing at the End of the World at Casa del Árbol.

One confirmed option is [“Ecuador, the Galápagos and Humpback Whales”](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/), in which the waterfall excursion takes place on **August 14, 2027**, on day four. After the excursion, travelers return to Quito and fly to the Galápagos Islands the following day.

After breakfast, you explore central Baños, then head to [Agoyán Waterfall](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/) and continue along the Pastaza River valley. The itinerary includes **Manto de la Novia** with a cable-car crossing, Pailón del Diablo, and the swings at [Casa del Árbol](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/). These are several outdoor stops, not a single waterfall viewed through a car window.

According to the full excursion itinerary, the day takes **11–12 hours**, including driving. The **Baños–Quito transfer takes about 3.5 hours**. Because it returns to the capital, this route is longer than the similar waterfall excursion that continues to Riobamba. The pace depends on the actual stops and road conditions.

At Pastaza Canyon, you may choose an optional **canopy zipline for $15 per person**. It is not included in the services covered by the excursion price. Other extreme sports advertised to visitors in Baños are not automatically part of this particular day.

The [11-day Galápagos itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/) takes in several natural regions of Ecuador. On the day before the waterfalls, the route visits Quilotoa and other mountain locations. On **August 14**, after Baños, the group returns to Quito and checks into the Finlandia 4* hotel, with breakfast included. On **August 15**, travelers fly to the Galápagos and visit Santa Cruz.

This sequence matters: returning to Quito makes the onward island flight possible without an additional overnight stay in Riobamba. If you are choosing a tour for its volcanic landscapes followed by the Galápagos, look at the complete day-by-day itinerary rather than searching only for “Waterfall Route” in the title.

## Two Versions of the Waterfall Route

| Excursion | Where You Go After Baños |

| [Returning to Quito](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) | Quito, about 3.5 hours by road |
| [Waterfalls and Swing](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) | Riobamba, about 2 hours |

Both programs visit Agoyán, Manto de la Novia, Pailón del Diablo, and Casa del Árbol. The main difference is **the direction of the onward journey**. The first returns to the capital; the second includes a night in Riobamba and can continue into the southern Andes.

These excursions should therefore not be treated as duplicates merely because they visit the same waterfalls. When choosing a tour, check where the day ends, how long it takes, and what begins the following morning.

Shoes with good grip and protection for belongings against spray will help on walks near the waterfalls. Follow local safety rules on cable crossings and at the swings. You do not have to add every possible activity: the main excursion is already a long day ending with a transfer.

For [nature tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/), bear in mind that a visit to Baños can take different forms: a short stop, a full day, or a transit stage in a longer journey. The canonical excursion module defines the exact stops.

## Baños: The Waterfall Route, the Swing at the End of the World, and Transfer to Riobamba

[Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) lies between the Andean slopes and Ecuador's humid valleys. The famous Waterfall Route begins here, where the Pastaza River cuts through the mountains and streams plunge over rocky ledges. This Ada Tours excursion combines a walk through the town, **three waterfalls**, the canyon, swings high above a mountainside, and an onward transfer to Riobamba.

The complete program takes **8–9 hours including transfers**. With several nature stops throughout the day, comfortable shoes and preparation for changeable mountain weather are advisable.

## How the Excursion Day Begins

After breakfast at the hotel, you explore central Baños. The town stands at the foot of Tungurahua Volcano, at an elevation of approximately **1,826 meters**, near forests, thermal springs, and deep river valleys.

The journey then follows the [Pastaza Valley](/ecuador/place/pastaza-canyon/). The road winds between green slopes, with waterfalls appearing one after another. The cascades are only part of the attraction: travelers also see the transition from the Andes to the more humid foothills and how the river has carved its gorge.

## Three Waterfalls on One Route

The first named stop is [Agoyán Waterfall](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), a powerful flow in the Pastaza Valley. Here you can clearly see how water descends steep hillsides into the depths of the canyon.

Next comes [Manto de la Novia, or Bride's Veil Waterfall](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/). Its name refers to the white ribbon of falling water, reminiscent of a bridal veil. We have included a **cable-car crossing** at this waterfall, providing a different perspective on the gorge.

Another stop is [Pailón del Diablo (Devil's Cauldron)](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/), where the torrent crashes against rocks with great force. Depending on the permitted path and weather conditions, visitors can get close enough to feel the spray.

Each of the three waterfalls has a different appearance and setting. The program therefore explores the valley through successive stops rather than visiting only one viewpoint. Be careful on wet paths: shoes with good grip are more useful here than lightweight city sneakers.

## Casa del Árbol and the Swings Above the Slope

After the waterfalls, the route visits [Casa del Árbol, home to the Swing at the End of the World](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/). The swings are famous for their views of the mountainside and surrounding peaks. The appeal lies in the height, open space, and unusual viewing angle.

Use of the swings depends on the weather and the venue's rules. It is especially important to follow staff instructions and avoid seeking dramatic photographs in unsafe places outside the permitted area.

Do not confuse this stop with the **canopy zipline over Pastaza Canyon**. You can add the canopy activity to your trip if you wish; it costs an additional **15 USD per person**. Participation depends on the attraction's operating conditions and individual restrictions. This fee does not automatically cover other activities in Baños.

## Transfer to Riobamba: Continuing the Journey

The program ends with a transfer to [Riobamba](/ecuador/place/riobamba/), taking approximately **2 hours**. Hotel accommodation and a free evening are planned. This makes the excursion suitable for a continuous itinerary across Ecuador: from Baños, the journey continues into the Andean highlands rather than returning to its starting point.

This matters when choosing a tour. If you want a short, standalone visit to the waterfalls followed by a return to Baños, compare the terms of that option separately: this itinerary includes the transfer to the next destination.

## Practical Details and Preparation

Baños has a fairly warm, humid climate, though rain can arrive quickly. Typical temperatures for Baños are **around +20 °C by day and +10 °C at night**. Bring a lightweight waterproof jacket, closed-toe shoes, water, and protection for your phone against spray.

The program includes the waterfalls, a town walk, the swings, and the transfer. The **optional canopy zipline** is a separately priced service. Admission tickets to specific attractions and the group size should be agreed when arranging the trip, as they are not listed individually. The excursion language is Russian.

For a longer trip through the country, explore [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and nature-focused itineraries in the [Adventure section](/interests/adventure/). If you are interested in the day after Riobamba, a logical continuation may be the separate [Chimborazo and Ingapirca excursion](/ecuador/chimborazo-reserve/chimborazo-and-ingapirca/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Waterfall Route

### How long is the excursion day?

**8–9 hours**, including stops and the transfer to Riobamba. The Baños–Riobamba drive itself takes about 2 hours.

### Which waterfalls are included?

[Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), [Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/), and [Pailón del Diablo](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/).

### How much does the canopy zipline cost?

The optional canopy zipline above Pastaza Canyon is listed at **15 USD per person**. This is the price of the optional activity, not the entire excursion.

### Do we return to Baños in the evening?

In this program, the day ends in Riobamba, with a hotel stay. Returning to Baños requires a different itinerary.

## Tours Featuring the Baños Waterfalls and the Swing at the End of the World

[Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) lies on the slopes of Tungurahua and is known for its road past waterfalls and the deep canyon of the Pastaza River. The [standalone “Waterfall Route and Swing at the End of the World” excursion](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) combines a town walk, stops at Agoyán, Manto de la Novia and Pailón del Diablo waterfalls, and a visit to **Casa del Árbol**.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include this excursion. One confirmed program is [“All of Ecuador for New Year: Andes and Galápagos”](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/). Its waterfall excursion is scheduled for **January 2, 2027**, on day four, after which the group heads to **Riobamba** for the night.

## What You'll See on the Road from Baños

The excursion begins with a short introduction to the town. The route then follows the Pastaza Valley. [Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/) impresses with its powerful flow among green slopes, Manto de la Novia features a cable-car crossing, and Pailón del Diablo is known for its strong waterfall in a narrow rocky gorge.

There is a separate stop at [the Swing at the End of the World](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/) at Casa del Árbol. The swings stand on a mountainside with panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Swing photographs are popular, but using the attraction depends on local rules and weather. The visit is part of the itinerary; other sporting activities are not automatically included.

The excursion day lasts **8–9 hours including transfers**. The drive from Baños to Riobamba takes approximately **2 hours**. An optional **canopy zipline over Pastaza Canyon costs an additional $15 per person**. Rafting, canyoning, and other activities are also available near Baños, but mentioning them does not mean they are included in this itinerary.

## How the Excursion Fits into the New Year Tour

[“All of Ecuador for New Year”](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) is an **11-day** journey through different parts of the country, including the Andes, Cuenca, and the Galápagos. Day four, **January 2, 2027**, takes travelers through Baños and its waterfalls. The day ends with a transfer to Riobamba and accommodation at **Hotel Casa Real 4***; breakfast is included under the day's arrangements.

The following day, the route continues through the Chimborazo Reserve and Ingapirca to Cuenca. It then heads toward the high-altitude Cajas National Park and a cocoa plantation, followed later by the Galápagos portion. The Riobamba transfer is thus an integral part of the journey across the Ecuadorian Andes, rather than an arbitrary extra added after the waterfalls.

The right option depends on your interests. For travelers seeking both mountain regions and the Galápagos, the Andean route makes it possible to discover several areas before flying to the islands. A different standalone excursion is available for those who would rather return to the capital after Baños.

## Baños to Riobamba or Baños to Quito?

| Excursion | Where the Day Continues |
|---|---|
| [Baños with Transfer to Riobamba](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) | Riobamba and an overnight stay |
| [Baños with Return to Quito](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) | Ecuador's capital |

The attractions are very similar, but **the final destination is fundamentally different**. The excursion described here takes **8–9 hours including transfers** and ends in Riobamba. In the version returning to Quito, the whole day lasts **11–12 hours** including transfers, with a final road journey of about 3.5 hours.

When booking, do not rely on the shared name “Waterfall Route”: the same nature stops may lead to different cities. In a complete tour, transfers and overnight stays are already linked to the subsequent itinerary and should be considered together.

## Who Will Enjoy This Excursion?

This day will appeal to travelers who enjoy waterfalls, green mountain valleys, and light adventure. Surfaces at some stops may be wet, so nonslip shoes and a waterproof layer are useful. Follow the local operators' instructions at the cable crossing and the swings. Participation in the canopy zipline is a separate choice.

For other nature-focused itineraries, explore [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and [trips through natural areas](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/), but compare the specific sequence of days.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Baños and Riobamba

### How long does the waterfall day take?

**8–9 hours** including transfers. The drive from Baños to Riobamba takes approximately 2 hours.

### On which day does the excursion take place in the New Year tour?

**January 2, 2027**, day four of the [New Year Ecuador itinerary](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/).

### Where do travelers spend the night after Baños?

In **Riobamba**, at Hotel Casa Real 4*.

### Which adventure activities cost extra?

An optional **canopy zipline at $15 per person** is available. No other sports are stated as included.

### Can we return directly to Quito?

There is a separate [route returning to Quito](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) with a different duration and end point.
